items.title: FDA issues Complete Response Letter for Summit ivonescimab application
items.summary: Summit confirmed the FDA cannot approve its current ivonescimab application for previously treated EGFR-mutated lung cancer. The FDA found that progression-free-survival benefit without statistically significant overall-survival improvement was insufficient. This delays near-term U.S. commercialization for the indication while other clinical studies continue.

observations.label: Decision, November 15
observations.value: FDA Complete Response Letter; BLA cannot be approved in present form

observations.label: Last regular-session SMMT close, November 13 at 4 PM EST
observations.value: $14.15, down 6.14%; before Sunday FDA decision, not a market reaction to it

observations.label: Fundamental significance
observations.value: U.S. launch delayed for this indication; broader clinical program continues

observations.label: Risks and next indicators
observations.value: FDA resubmission conditions, overall-survival results from HARMONi-3 and other trials, funding, Monday price/volume; compelling new survival evidence could soften setback

items.key_finding: Confirmed FDA rejection materially delays Summit's U.S. ivonescimab commercialization in this indication.

items.title: Yemeni government forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb positions, increasing Houthi leverage over Red Sea shipping
items.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces announced withdrawal from positions near Dhubab and Bab el-Mandeb, redeploying toward Aden. Reuters and the Financial Times corroborate the territorial change, which increases Houthi leverage over a major shipping chokepoint. No incremental vessel damage, closure or export loss from this withdrawal has been independently verified.

observations.label: Military development November 15
observations.value: Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces announced withdrawal from Dhubab Airport and Bab el-Mandeb positions toward Aden; Reuters and FT report increased Houthi control/influence

observations.label: Physical-flow confirmation
observations.value: No additional commercial transit closure or incremental oil-export disruption attributable to the withdrawal independently established

observations.label: Latest benchmark context
observations.value: Brent Friday November 13 settlement $95.84 per barrel; not a Sunday market reaction

observations.label: Risk and next indicators
observations.value: UKMTO incident reports, Red Sea transits, war-risk insurance, Saudi Yanbu exports, and next Brent session; safe sustained passage or reversal of territorial control weakens impact

items.key_finding: Corroborated territorial withdrawal near Bab el-Mandeb increases dual-chokepoint shipping risk without yet proving new physical export losses.

items.title: Anthropic IPO filings expose long-dated AI infrastructure commitments and strategic financing dependence
items.summary: Anthropic's November 10 amended SEC prospectus discloses $900.9 billion of long-term infrastructure purchase and lease commitments, including $70.7 billion due within the next 12 months. Its proposed IPO is accompanied by a conditional $26 billion equity placement among major AI technology suppliers. Strong revenue growth contrasts with substantial future cash requirements and complex supplier-customer financing relationships.

observations.label: Preliminary IPO terms
observations.value: 825 million Class A shares offered, indicated $70-$78 each; Nasdaq symbol ANT applied for; pricing and trading date not final

observations.label: Infrastructure and compute commitment
observations.value: Approximately $900.9 billion in contractual commitments and leases, predominantly through 2045; approximately $451.6 billion expected before December 31, 2030

observations.label: Near-term obligations
observations.value: Approximately $70.7 billion due in the 12 months following September 30, 2026

observations.label: Conditional strategic placement
observations.value: $26.0 billion of Class N equity after IPO closing, subject to conditions; Nvidia and Google $10.0 billion each, AMD $2.5 billion, other named chip/software partners; some overlap previous financing commitments

observations.label: Business run rate
observations.value: Approximately $81 billion annualized revenue run rate as of October 31, 2026, as reported by Anthropic

observations.label: Next evidence and invalidation
observations.value: Final IPO pricing, offering proceeds and placement completion; Nvidia November 17 results at 5 p.m. EST; postponement, lower funding, weaker revenue/AI infrastructure demand would weaken confidence

items.key_finding: Anthropic's verified IPO filing exposes unprecedented long-term compute obligations tied to conditional supplier-backed equity funding.

items.title: FAA says L3Harris network upgrade work preceded nationwide ground stop; LHX falls in Friday after-hours
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Duffy identified L3Harris as the contractor replacing copper links with fiber when a router flooded FAA air-traffic communications and radar networks. Officials have not determined whether installation error or defective equipment caused the disruption. LHX fell roughly 3.8%-4.2% in Friday extended trading, while thousands more flights were canceled Saturday.

items.title: Chinese AI developers sink while domestic chipmaker Cambricon rises on U.S. export-access fears
items.summary: Friday's Hong Kong close saw Z.ai fall about 10.9% and MiniMax 8.2%, while Cambricon's Shanghai shares gained 21.9% over five sessions. Reuters and FT link the divergence to concerns that tighter U.S. export and offshore-compute controls could constrain Chinese AI developers. Domestic chip capacity and actual rulemaking remain critical uncertainties.

observations.value: About -10.9% Friday; Friday local-market move, not a November 14 live quote; Reuters and FT
